answer: The applicant posts a 3,500 POA bond and brings one hand-dyed violet thread to a staffed inlet warehouse marked as the day's haven (address posted at 06:00). A clerk measures the strand against a published 0.4 mm gauge, blots a fresh dye-bleed onto numbered paper, then sews that same thread through a one-use lead seal tagged with a single pubkey. A machine-spun substitute, a dried or swapped strand, a second key on the same seal, or arrival at any other site slashes the bond and retires the seal. Mailed spools and photos of someone else's stitching are refused.
